document_title: How USDA uses AI to pick screwworm surveillance and sterile fly release sites in Texas

3.headline: 43 premises. 17 counties.
3.dek: The Texas Animal Health Commission counts 43 Texas premises with at least one confirmed detection, across 17 counties. One windmill is one premises. Drawn to illustrate.

4.headline: The models pick the place
4.dek: USDA's research service has models that use AI to predict where the fly is likely to take hold. They already pick areas for surveillance, fly trapping and sterile fly releases, says Kim Lohmeyer, who directs the Kerrville laboratory. Drawn to illustrate.

7.headline: More than 36,000 seen. No case among them.
7.dek: USDA's drones flew over Texas more than 2,000 times since June, KRGV reported. They found no case among the more than 36,000 animals observed. Officials called the drones not foolproof. One animal is a thousand seen. Drawn to illustrate.

8.headline: The trailer the models can't predict
8.dek: The models can't predict every scenario, Kim Lohmeyer says. Lohmeyer names one above all, people moving infested animals. Drawn to illustrate.
